title: Evaluate a cubic at an integer (factor theorem test)
source: P23 Ch1 theory P23-1.5 Quick check 1 (f(4)=0 for x^3-6x^2+5x+12)

contexts.stem: To test a possible factor of \(x^3+({p|int})x^2+({q|int})x+({r|int})\) by the factor theorem, evaluate the cubic at \(x={c|int}\).
The polynomial \(x^3+({p|int})x^2+({q|int})x+({r|int})\) is denoted by \(f(x)\). Find \(f({c|int})\).

title: The value of c when f(c)=0 for the factor x-c
source: P23 Ch1 theory P23-1.5 Quick check 2 (f(-5)=0 so c=-5 in the factor x-c)
stem: It is given that \(f({c|int})=0\). In the linear factor \(x-c\) of \(f(x)\), what is the value of \(c\)?

steps.name: form
steps.text_tex: By the factor theorem, \(x-c\) is a factor when \(f(c)=0\).

contexts.stem: A polynomial satisfies \(f({c|int})=0\). What value of \(c\) appears in the monic linear factor \(x-c\)?
The factor theorem is to be applied to a polynomial with \(f({c|int})=0\). What is the value of \(c\) in the factor \(x-c\)?

title: Coefficient of x in the factor ax-b when f(b/a)=0
source: P23 Ch1 theory P23-1.5 Quick check 3 (f(2/3)=0, factor 3x-2, coefficient 3)
stem: It is given that \(f\bigl(\dfrac{{{b|int}}}{{{a|int}}}\bigr)=0\). What is the coefficient of \(x\) in the linear factor \(ax-b\) of \(f(x)\), where \(a\) and \(b\) are coprime positive integers?

steps.name: form
steps.text_tex: The extended factor theorem gives the factor \({a|int}x-{b|int}\).
steps.note: Use P(b/a)=0 implies ax-b is a factor.

contexts.stem: A polynomial satisfies \(f({b|int}/{a|int})=0\). In the factor \(ax-b\) with coprime positive integers \(a\) and \(b\), what is the value of \(a\)?
By the extended factor theorem, \(f\bigl(\dfrac{{{b|int}}}{{{a|int}}}\bigr)=0\) gives a factor \(ax-b\). What is the coefficient of \(x\)?

title: Show that 2x+3 is a factor of 8x^3+4x^2-10x+3

source.note: Stem verbatim from the QP PDF, part (i) only. Later parts of Q7 are omitted. Fully manual show-that. Independently, substituting x=-3/2 gives 0, so 2x+3 is a factor. Steps from the official MS PDF.

stem: Use the factor theorem to show that \(2x+3\) is a factor of \(8x^3+4x^2-10x+3\).

steps.name: conc
steps.text_tex: The value is \(8\bigl(-\dfrac{27}{8}\bigr)+4\bigl(\dfrac{9}{4}\bigr)-10\bigl(-\dfrac{3}{2}\bigr)+3=-27+9+15+3=0\). Hence \(2x+3\) is a factor.
steps.note: MS: conclusion that it is a factor.

title: Show that x+3 is a factor of 4x^3+4x^2-29x-15

source.note: Stem verbatim from the QP PDF, part (i) only. Part (ii) (complete factorisation) is omitted so that this item stays with the factor theorem test. Fully manual show-that. Independently, f(-3)=-108+36+87-15=0. Steps from the official MS PDF.

stem: The polynomial \(p(x)\) is defined by \(p(x)=4x^3+4x^2-29x-15\). Use the factor theorem to show that \(x+3\) is a factor of \(p(x)\).

steps.name: conc
steps.note: MS: Obtain -108+36+87-15=0 or equivalent and conclude.
